user.title: Set up Brilliant MQTT
user.description: Choose where the Brilliant panels should connect. The recommended path uses the official Home Assistant Mosquitto broker add-on; an existing or externally hosted MQTT broker is also fully supported.

menu_options.existing_broker: Existing or external MQTT broker (fully supported)

official_mosquitto.title: Home Assistant Mosquitto add-on (recommended)
official_mosquitto.description: Use the official `core_mosquitto` add-on. Install and start the add-on first, then create dedicated Brilliant broker credentials for the panels. Home Assistant's existing MQTT connection is validated separately.

existing_broker.title: Existing or external MQTT broker
existing_broker.description: Use any reachable MQTT broker, including one hosted outside Home Assistant. The integration validates connectivity and required broker behavior before it changes a panel.

broker.title: Validate MQTT broker
broker.description: For the recommended Home Assistant path, install and start the official `core_mosquitto` add-on, then create dedicated Brilliant broker credentials before continuing. External-broker users do not need this add-on; enter a broker address reachable by Home Assistant and every Brilliant panel. Advanced settings are optional.

data_description.mqtt_host: Address reachable by both Home Assistant and every Brilliant panel.
data_description.mqtt_port: Usually 1883 without TLS or 8883 with TLS.
data_description.mqtt_username: Broker account used by the Brilliant fleet.
data_description.mqtt_password: Broker password. It is stored securely and is never shown again.

data_description.mqtt_tls_ca: Optional public PEM certificate chain for a private broker CA. Never paste a private key.

script.title: Panel settings
script.description: Name the panel, choose its components, and configure the Home Assistant-owned control plane. Global control settings are shared by every Brilliant panel.

data_description.name: A friendly name, e.g. "Office Bath". A lowercase id is derived for MQTT topics ("Office Bath" → office-bath).
data_description.mesh_priority: 0 = this panel never publishes the BLE mesh. Among positive values the LOWEST wins leader election (1 = primary, 2/3 = standbys).
data_description.voice: Install a Home Assistant voice satellite on this panel (on-panel wake word + microphone + speaker). Speech-to-text, the conversation agent, and text-to-speech all run in your HA Assist pipeline — nothing voice-specific is configured on the panel.
data_description.voice_wake_word: The on-panel wake word that activates the satellite.
data_description.voice_ha_host: Only needed if the panel cannot resolve your Home Assistant URL's hostname (e.g. a segmented IoT VLAN). Format: hostname=ip, e.g. homeassistant.example=10.0.0.5. Leave blank to use the panel's own DNS.
data_description.wifi_watchdog: Auto-recovers lost Wi-Fi (reconnect → restart networking → reboot the panel as a last resort).
data_description.bus_watchdog: Installs the on-panel daemon that reboots the panel if the Brilliant bus stays wedged for 30+ minutes.
data_description.hue_ca: Installs a periodic timer that re-injects your diyHue CA certificate into the panel's pinned Hue trust bundle, recovering it after an OTA update wipes /data.
data_description.hue_ca_cert: The diyHue bridge's CA certificate, PEM-encoded. Required to enable Hue CA recovery.
data_description.ha_control_enabled: Publishes a constrained, local MQTT control manifest from Home Assistant. The legacy on-panel HA mirror remains disabled.
data_description.ha_control_label: Home Assistant label selecting entities for the constrained control manifest.
data_description.room_overrides: A JSON object mapping Home Assistant area names to Brilliant room names, for example {"Office":"Office Bath"}.
data_description.ha_control_domains: Only selected supported domains enter the control manifest.
data_description.max_mirrored_entities: Safety limit for entities in the control manifest (1–200).
data_description.scene_panel: Brilliant panel used when a scene or mode service call omits a panel.
data_description.scene_actions: A JSON object of explicitly allowlisted scene actions keyed by panel and scene ID.

reconfigure.description: Edit this panel and the fleet-wide Home Assistant control settings. Panel changes are pushed over SSH; global settings are copied to every Brilliant entry.

progress.broker_validation: Checking Home Assistant MQTT readiness, broker authentication, discovery writes, and retained-message behavior.

error.reserved_panel: "mesh" is the reserved whole-home pseudo-panel and cannot be managed.
error.invalid_name: Enter a name with at least one letter or digit.
error.invalid_value: Control characters are not allowed in this field.
error.config_entry_storage_unavailable: Home Assistant could not confirm the fleet in durable storage. Check storage health and try again; no panel changes were made.
error.mesh_priority_exhausted: All supported mesh priorities are already assigned. Remove an unused panel before adding another.
error.ha_mqtt_unavailable: Home Assistant's MQTT integration is not ready. Install/configure MQTT, verify the broker connection, and retry.
error.unsupported_discovery_prefix: The configured MQTT discovery prefix is unsupported. Restore a valid Home Assistant discovery prefix and retry.
error.broker_validation_failed: MQTT validation failed unexpectedly. Verify the broker connection and credentials, then retry.
error.broker_connect_failed: Could not connect to the MQTT broker. Verify host, port, routing, and firewall rules.
error.broker_tls_verification_failed: The MQTT broker certificate could not be verified. Check the broker certificate and optional public CA chain.
error.broker_timeout: The MQTT broker did not respond in time.
error.broker_authentication_failed: The MQTT broker rejected these credentials.
error.broker_connection_rejected: The MQTT broker rejected the connection settings.
error.fleet_auth_failed: The MQTT broker rejected the fleet credentials.
error.panel_to_ha_timeout: No panel-to-Home Assistant validation message arrived. Confirm both systems use the same broker and that broker ACLs allow the fleet topics.
error.ha_to_panel_timeout: No Home Assistant-to-panel validation message arrived. Confirm the panel can reach this broker and that broker ACLs allow the fleet topics.
error.discovery_write_denied: The broker denied the MQTT discovery validation write. Update its ACLs and retry.
error.discovery_write_timeout: The MQTT discovery validation write timed out. Check broker routing and ACLs.
error.retained_message_invalid: The broker did not preserve the validation message correctly. Verify retained-message support.
error.retained_message_timeout: Retained-message validation timed out. Verify broker retention behavior and routing.
error.cleanup_failed: MQTT validation cleanup did not finish. Review broker connectivity before retrying.
error.operation_failed: MQTT validation failed. Review the integration documentation and retry.
error.cannot_connect: SSH connection failed — check the host and the root password.
error.cannot_read_config: The agent is installed but its configuration could not be read. Try Reconfigure, or remove and re-add the panel.
error.cannot_apply: Connected, but writing the new settings to the panel failed. Check the agent and try Repair.
error.cannot_install: Connected, but installing the agent on the panel failed. Check the panel and try again.
error.cannot_install_voice: The bridge agent installed, but installing the voice satellite failed (its payload may not be downloadable yet, or the panel rejected it). Untick "Enable voice satellite" to finish without it, or try again.
error.wrong_panel: That host already runs a different Brilliant panel's agent. Check the IP — applying here would overwrite and restart the wrong panel.
error.host_key_changed: The panel's SSH host key changed since it was added. If this is expected (e.g. the panel was reflashed), remove and re-add the panel to re-pin it. Otherwise it may indicate a man-in-the-middle, so do not proceed until you have confirmed the host.

panel_connect.title: Connect to a Brilliant panel
panel_connect.description: Enter the panel address and root password. Home Assistant first reads and verifies the panel identity; installation starts only after you review the detected panel.

data_description.host: A stable address reachable from Home Assistant.
data_description.root_password: Used only for this panel's pinned SSH connection and stored per panel.

panel_confirm.title: Confirm Brilliant panel
panel_confirm.description: Detected `{hostname}` ({model}, {architecture}) with SSH fingerprint `{fingerprint}`. Name the panel to continue. Home Assistant will verify durable fleet storage before making any panel changes.

data_description.name: A friendly name used in Home Assistant. A stable MQTT slug is allocated automatically.

data.auto_repair: Automatically repair the bridge after an outage

data_description.trust_host_key_changes: When on, repair auto-trusts a changed SSH host key so a firmware update that rotates the panel's keys recovers hands-off. This offers the root password to whatever host answers at the panel's address, so only enable on a trusted/isolated network (e.g. a firewalled IoT VLAN). Each automatic re-pin fires a host_key_repinned event you can alert on. Default off: a changed key instead surfaces repair_failed (host_key_changed) and asks you to Reconfigure to re-pin.

repair.name: Repair bridge
repair.description: Restore the unit/env from known-good sources, install the agent if it's missing, and start it.

redeploy.name: Redeploy agent
redeploy.description: Force-push the bundled agent payload and restart the bridge.

uninstall.name: Uninstall agent
uninstall.description: Stop, disable, and remove the agent from the panel (explicit only).

reboot.name: Reboot panel
reboot.description: Capture a diagnostics bundle over SSH, then reboot the panel. The panel's logs are volatile (lost on reboot), so diagnostics are always captured first.

collect_diagnostics.name: Capture diagnostics
collect_diagnostics.description: Capture a diagnostics bundle before rebooting (saved under the config directory).

journal_lines.name: Journal lines
journal_lines.description: How many current-boot journal lines to capture.

run_scene.name: Run Brilliant scene
run_scene.description: Run a scene on an attached Brilliant panel and wait for execution confirmation.

panel.name: Panel
panel.description: Attached panel slug. Omit it to use the configured scene panel.

scene_id.name: Scene ID
scene_id.description: Stable scene ID from the selected panel's current catalog.

set_mode.name: Set Brilliant mode
set_mode.description: Set a mode on an attached Brilliant panel and wait for execution confirmation.

panel.name: Panel
panel.description: Attached panel slug. Omit it to use the configured scene panel.

mode_id.name: Mode ID
mode_id.description: Stable mode ID from the selected panel's current catalog.

already_in_progress.message: A repair or update is already in progress for this panel.

host_key_changed.message: The panel SSH host key changed. If this is expected (e.g. a reflash), remove and re-add the panel to re-pin it, or enable "Trust host-key changes" in options for hands-off repair. If unexpected, investigate before proceeding.

needs_attention.title: Brilliant panel needs attention
needs_attention.description: Panel `{panel}` needs attention: {reason}. This issue clears automatically once the bridge recovers.

voice_missing.title: Brilliant panel voice satellite not installed
voice_missing.description: Panel `{panel}` has the voice satellite enabled but it isn't running. This issue clears automatically once the satellite is deployed (run Repair, or wait for the next automatic repair).

ha_mirror_retired.title: Legacy Brilliant HA mirror disabled
ha_mirror_retired.description: Panel `{panel}` still has legacy HA mirror state. {reason}. The integration will keep retrying safe removal during panel management; legacy credentials are retained until absence is verified.
